full_judgment: 14. All the P.Ws. made their statements before the Court regarding the alleged forged document on presumption, surmise and doubts but none of them witnessed the actual making, signing or executing the said deed. This aspect of the evidence was totally overlooked by the Courts below. In order to prove a document as forged, the ingredients of sections 463 and 464 of the Penal Code must be proved first which the prosecution has totally failed, Further document shall be called a forged document if it is made or executed with dishonest and fraudulent intention to defraud other persons. Such finding is also absent in the judgments of the Courts below. Rather, the case of the accused petitioners is that they purchased it bonafide, before the purchase of the complainant, from the recorded owner Rai Charan Barman whose father was Rain Kumar @ Ananda Lal Barman, which is supported by the old and new records of right Ext. B series. In this view of the matter I find that the prosecution could not prove the elements of a forged document in the present case and as such the provisions of section 467 of the Penal Code cannot be invoked against the accused petitioners.
